text: When designing a REST API, it is important to follow best practices to ensure it is easy to use and maintain. First, use clear and descriptive endpoints like `/users` or `/products` instead of vague names. Status codes are also essential — for example, `200` for success, `404` for not found, and `500` for server errors. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use the API quickly. Finally, consider using versioning, such as `/v1/users`, so that updates do not break existing code. These simple steps make your API more reliable and user-friendly.
